quest.title: As the Sun Rises and Sets
quest.description: The time for the meeting has finally come. Head over to the Speaker's Chamber.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1425, Primogem x30, Mora x62225, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x11

talks.objective: Go to the Speaker's Chamber to meet Mavuika

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I see. If all goes well, three days should be more than enough to forge the name. You won't need to push back the plan.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Thank you. I'd say the sooner you can finish it, the better. I still need to announce the matter to everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #Don't worry. We should only need half a day. {NICKNAME} has been in Natlan a while, now. The Pilgrim's Chronicle should have enough records of {M#his}{F#her} adventures.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Come in.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Mavuika! Oh, Xilonen and Citlali are here too! Hello!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: #We were just talking about you. I invited you here for two reasons. First, there's {NICKNAME}'s Ancient Name, which is ready to be forged.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah! You need the Pilgrim's Chronicle, right? The device the Lord of the Night gave us.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I brought it with me.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Perfect. Could I take a look?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Hmm... Yep.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Looks good. This is definitely enough to work with.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Usually, the first step to forging an Ancient Name is performing a ceremony to extract memories from the Ley Lines. But, since the Lord of the Night gave us this record, we can skip that part.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Still, I've never used something like this before. This is an entirely new material for me, so I need to look into how the process might change.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I'll help you. My knowledge on the Lord of the Night and the Wayob might come in handy.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That brings me to the second matter. As you already know, once your Ancient Name is complete, we need to venture into the deepest part of the Night Kingdom.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That will happen in three days' time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Th—Three days!? So soon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait! But, um...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: #You're worried about {NICKNAME}, aren't you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, Paimon gave it a lot of thought, and Paimon's not very good at thinking or fighting to begin with. It's just...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This plan could save countless lives. Paimon understands why people would want to be a part of something so important...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #But... all this time, Paimon has barely left {NICKNAME}'s side. Not to mention, we all know this will be a super dangerous mission...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: That's right. And, as long as we win, the Ode of Resurrection will return us to this land.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: The Night Kingdom is a realm of souls and memories, where mental fortitude outweighs physical strength.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: All in Natlan are resolved to win this war. The Sacred Flame will connect us to their fighting spirit. We will do whatever it takes to win.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: #So, if you want to contribute, just cheer us on alongside all the people of Natlan. For {NICKNAME}, I'm sure your words of encouragement are among the most important.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The most important? Really...?

choices.text: That way, it'd be like we're still together.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! Overcoming danger side by side, just like always!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, it's decided! Paimon will cheer the loudest out of everyone in Natlan!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: It's less about volume, and more about mental focus. But, I get it. You're just trying to show how much you care.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Of course, this all depends on the successful completion of the Ancient Name.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: #Otherwise, {NICKNAME} will not join me. That is the condition.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Don't worry. I swear on the honor of my tribe — I will not fail. I know how important this is.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: There's no time to lose. Let's go.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Alright, everyone. When we meet again, it will be to deliver the Ancient Name.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good luck, you two!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Three days, huh... What should we do in the meantime? We know you're still rebuilding, so is there anything we can do to help?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: From what I've heard, the two of you have helped more than enough. You should take a well-deserved rest.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Even if there are stray Abyss monsters out there, our warriors can handle them. Don't worry.

choices.text: Still, if things haven't returned to normal...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly! We can't take a break! We're adventurers! We've gotta live up to the name!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We still have a long journey ahead of us and so many places to go! The battle in three days is just another part of our adventure!

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Haha, I see. In that case, just do what you think is best.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What about you?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: This final battle is extremely important to me — the culmination of my life's work. Still, I think you've got the right idea.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: I'm also going to follow my heart. I plan on using these three days to calm my mind and work on a painting.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh? You know how to paint?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: I just learned, actually. I hear it takes a lot of practice to get any good.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: It could be anything, though. What I really enjoy is the process of getting better at something through practice. It's how I relax.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Of course, that's only when I have the time. I'm usually too busy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, that's how you relax... Well, it definitely seems like your style.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We'll leave you to it, then.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Alright. Let's go our separate ways for now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, if Mavuika relaxes by working really hard at something... That basically means she never takes a break, right? Wow, she's definitely something else...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, uh... hello? Sorry, Mavuika's not here right now.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: There you are!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: *panting*... We made it.

choices.text: Why are you so out of breath?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Haha, other than our plan almost falling through? Nothing at all!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: The preparations took longer than expected. We were so worried we wouldn't make it before you left on your next big adventure.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Well, if you hadn't overslept...

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Details, details. Anyway, come on! Let's go to the People of the Springs!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hold on! Tell us what's going on first.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Oh, yeah, haha. Jumped the gun a bit there, didn't I? Basically, we know about your super important mission coming up, and we want to give you a proper send-off!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Before the Pilgrimage, we usually hold a huge feast! All you can eat, with meat by the tableful!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh! All you can eat!?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: I knew that would pique your interest, Paimon. You can eat to your heart's content. You won't wanna miss out, I promise!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Of course, there's not just meat, but also all kinds of fruit, vegetables, desserts, drinks, you name it! You won't be disappointed!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That sounds amazing! We're in!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Didn't you just say we need to live up to our title as adventurers?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, the best adventurers know how to go with the flow, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Plus, it sounds like this feast is in your honor. If you don't show up, everyone's hard work will be for nothing!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: It's our fault for not telling you earlier, so it's okay if you can't make it. Still, if you're not busy, we'd really like you to be there. It won't take up too much of your time!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: It'll be super fun! Plus, all our friends will be there.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Okay!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: YES! Let's go eat!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Huh? What's the hold up, {NICKNAME}? Did you think of something?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why don't we invite Mavuika?

response.speaker: Paimon & Kachina & Mualani
response.text: Huh!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: I—Isn't she painting?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Is that okay? It's not like we prepared anything fancy...

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: W—Well, I definitely wasn't expecting that suggestion. She's the Archon, after all. Maybe it's not our place...

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: But, we might as well extend the invitation! The Archon is about to fight for us with everything she has! This feast is in her honor, too!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Um, then who's gonna be the one to invite her?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: All of us, of course!

choices.text: That way, I'll always remember how much you care about me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay... then, please don't do anything reckless! That's what Paimon's trying to avoid!

choices.text: That way, it'll be just like fishing with you cheering me on.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, not sure what fishing has to do with anything, but... If you're making weird analogies, guess that means you're not nervous.

choices.text: We have to be the ones to do this.

talks.objective: Invite Mavuika to come along with you

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Come in.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you four. Is there something you need?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're here to invite you to the People of the Springs for a feast!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Ah, I see. This is a special kind of feast, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Exactly! It's a tradition to hold a feast before battle! We couldn't miss out on this opportunity. It's our way of cheering you on!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Plus, I always wanted to do something to thank you for saving me from the Night Kingdom...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That was my duty. Besides, it's all in the past now. You don't owe me anything.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Although, this feast does sound rather interesting.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: So, you'll come?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Of course. No need to notify Amina in advance. I'll just surprise her, haha.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: You don't need to turn this into some kind of grand banquet on my account.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I'll try my best to attend as an ordinary person, not an Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's not like you're the type to pull rank or something.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: True, but my presence changes the way people act. I just don't want to spoil the fun — a lot of things can change once an Archon is involved.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Barbecue is best fresh off the grill. And still, people will insist on waiting for me to eat first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah... Paimon can see that...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I'll jump in if that happens! I can throw manners to the wind, no problem!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: No need, I can take care of it. Anyway, thank you for inviting me. It really means a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What about your painting?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I don't need to finish it. I enjoy the process, but now there's something more interesting to do.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Th—Then, let's go together! The main dish should be ready soon!

talks.objective: Go to the People of the Springs

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Amina, there's been another delivery.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: You're kidding! ANOTHER one?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Just like the others — they heard about the feast and wanted to send something to contribute.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: But, this is just a small send-off. What are we going to do with all this stuff?

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Then again, I understand where they're coming from... I'll deal with it. *sigh* What a headache... If this continues, half of this stuff's gonna go bad before we get to it...

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: HUH!? You... you're here already!? And you've even brought the...

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: A—Archon!? What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: We invited her! She agreed to come as a surprise guest!

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Surprise is putting it lightly... Sorry, sorry. I'm happy you're here, it's just...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: No apology necessary. What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Well, I started spreading the word about the send-off, just around the area, like usual. A lot of people are still busy repairing their homes, so I didn't think many people would come.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: But, the turnout has been overwhelming. Not to mention, we've received a small mountain of deliveries. There's no way we can use all this stuff.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: That's our Star Outlander's popularity for you!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, you remember that nickname...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're saying... everyone's here because of us?

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Yep! The news about your impending mission with the Pyro Archon has spread all over Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Plus, you were amazing in the recent battle. A lot of people are here just to thank you, or wish you good luck.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Basically, this whole thing is happening because so many people wanted to see you.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Still, we definitely weren't expecting you to show up with the Pyro Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It was my idea.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Yeah! Mavuika and {NICKNAME} are in this together! They both deserve a celebration.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Well, this is the perfect excuse to throw an even bigger party! All this extra stuff was gonna go to waste, anyway...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: No need to go to all that trouble on my account. That's not why I'm here.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Besides, with so much of our nation in ruins, resources are still scarce. Extra spending for my sake is the last thing we need.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: That's true...

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: *sigh* Party-planning isn't easy. I can handle the big picture, but I'm not used to dealing with the finer details. That was always Auntie Atea's job...

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Sorry, I'm just feeling a bit in over my head.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, speaking of Atea, how is she? Is she feeling any better?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Actually, there's something we haven't told you...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Auntie Atea passed away not long after the attack on our tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...What?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: When you brought me her talisman, I knew her end was near. Luckily, I got the chance to see her one last time.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: She was a hero to the very end. Even though her body was at its breaking point, she showed no pain or sorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: In her final moments, her thoughts were entirely with her tribe and her people.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Gatherings like this remind me of her and the parties she loved to organize. So, I decided to attend in her memory.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, you already knew...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: We didn't mean to hide anything from you. It's just... there was never a good time to bring it up.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Cheer up, everyone! Auntie Atea wouldn't want us to remember her with tears!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Parties like this were her specialty, but now it's up to us to carry on her legacy! So, we can't let her down — believe me, she has high standards!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that sounds about right...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: So, come on, let's get to work, everyone! Oh, uh... Chief Amina and our guests of honor excluded! Kachina, Kinich, time to go!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Wait, you don't have to drag me...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Amina, you mentioned something about a surplus of supplies. I may have a solution...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: First, invite anyone who comes to deliver supplies to stay for the gathering.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: If it's a caravan, ask them to extend an invitation to the sender, as well.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Make it clear in the invitation that anyone is welcome to attend, but you're no longer accepting donations.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: In addition, all leftover supplies will be purchased by the Speaker's Chamber, sorted, and donated to the appropriate areas.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Th—That would be such a big help, Archon! Thank you!

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: I'll get on it, right away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Amazing plan, Mavuika! It was clear, concise, and organized... But, uh, weren't you trying to keep this small?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I don't mind increasing the size of the gathering, I just didn't want it to be because of me.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: My approach to problem-solving is always the same. Different solutions lead to different outcomes. The method may change, but the "right choice" is always grounded in logic and reason.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, Paimon feels like she just learned a thing or two!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, should we take a walk while everyone finishes the preparations?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I mean, we are the guests of honor.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Sounds good. A casual stroll can be hard to come by. Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Mualani, it's almost time for the feast!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Maybe we should send the drinks out first? There's a bunch of guests here already.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Yep, yep! I'm making the juice as we speak... Oh, right! The ice!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Huh!? Oh, you scared me! Sorry, we're a little busy in the kitchen right now, but the food is almost ready!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: AJAW! Get out of the ice bucket!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: The Almighty Dragonlord K'uhul Ajaw will not tolerate this stifling hut! We seek a cool place of repose. This bucket suits our taste.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Great, now we can't use any of this ice. HEY! This is your mess! Get back here!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Kachina, Ajaw is on the run. Help me catch him!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: O—Okay...! Sorry, I gotta help with Ajaw.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: As usual, Ajaw brings chaos wherever he goes.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Lively, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Leave this to me, Kachina.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: What is this? Who dares lay a hand on the Almighty... Tch, Mavuika.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I got him, Mualani.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Expert Ajaw-wrangling, Archon! Thank you!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: You shall utter our name with more reverence! Or we shall... or I'll get Kinich to... ask you to apologize.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Some dragonlord you are, if you need your "servant" to protect you...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Ajaw ruined an entire bucket of ice. We have others, but still... That was not cool! How should he be punished, Archon?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Let me think...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Seems like you could use some extra hands around here. Ajaw, help out in the kitchen.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: What? The Almighty Dragonlord K'uhul Ajaw shall not be reduced to a menial kitchen laborer...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I wasn't asking.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: ...Understood.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Ajaw, you have to learn to be good at some point.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Well? Hop to it! There's a pile of vegetables with your name on it! You need to wash every leaf!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: H—Help! Someone save meeeeee!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Hm, this box is missing a label... Oh, it's you. What's up?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nothing! We're just taking a look around!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What have you been up to?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Well, everyone's busy rebuilding the tribes, so there's not a lot of saurian hunting work out there.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: But, the Pyro Archon assigned me a special mission.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, really?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That's a bit of an exaggeration — I just asked Kinich to help identify some of the unknown casualties from the battle.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The fighting consumed all of Natlan. Countless humans and saurians were dragged into the conflict. So, a lot of investigative work is required to confirm their identities.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Just like a detective, I only have tiny details to work with. The goal is to deduce their habits and find evidence to corroborate their identity.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: It's tricky work, but we have every reason to keep going.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Because Natlan's heroes deserve to be remembered... right?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Exactly. That is how we, as the living, respect our heroes and the value of their lives.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: So, let me know if you need extra help, Kinich.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I'm doing fine for now. The teams searching for the fallen need the help more than me. The longer we take to find the dead, the harder it will be to piece things together.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Understood. Thank you for your hard work.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Just doing my part.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: #Oh, {M#Gramps}{F#other Granny}, Archon... I swear, I've been on my best behavior recently.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* Paimon knows it's just how you talk, but you've gotta realize how suspicious that sounds, right?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Haha, I am curious, though... Are you still working with The Captain?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: No, I don't have a reason to follow him anymore, so my life is back to normal — growing vegetables, raising aphids...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Well, maybe not completely normal. I'm still keeping tabs on the situation in the Night Kingdom... The Ley Lines are in a bad state.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: We plan on bringing that to an end.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: #I know. You... and {M#Gramps}{F#other Granny}, right?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: You're going to become great heroes, and the most I can do is... weave a scroll of your deeds.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you know how to do that?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Most people from my tribe know the art, but I'm not very good... I can never seem to empty my mind.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: We commemorate the deeds of others as a form of inspiration. But, rather than waiting for someone else to be inspired, isn't it faster to just take things into your own hands?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well... There are always things we can't do on our own.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I wouldn't phrase it quite like that, but Paimon's not wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Time will give you an answer. I know how you feel, Ororon. It took me a long time to find my place in the world.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I'm more mature now, but that passion, that drive to prove myself... I miss it sometimes. Maybe you'll change in the future, but you can still be proud of who you are now.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: You're saying... I need to live in the present?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just do what you think is right.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Hm... Thank you, Archon. That's what I've always tried to do.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Hello, you guys! Sorry for the wait. We're still setting up the venue.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Hey, did I say you could take a break!? Keep pushing! This is the home stretch, and then we get to feast!

dialogues.speaker: Huaccue
dialogues.text: Yes, Coach!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you still helping rebuild the tribes?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: That work is pretty much done, but I've discovered a lot more people with Abyssal Corrosion Syndrome in the process.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: So, I've been compiling patient records while helping them overcome the hallucinations. Thanks to The Captain, we have the Draught of Lucidity for the worst cases.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I heard about your efforts. The Speaker's Chamber can take it from here.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: It's more effective to have a focused task force, and the Speaker's Chamber can contact the Fatui directly for more doses.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: The doctors at the Stadium aren't too busy?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: The worst is over, so it should be fine. I'll confirm it myself later.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I'll be in touch with next steps. I just need you to compile all existing patient records to ease the transition.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Understood, Archon! Although, I'd like to continue helping out with the treatment. I can't let everything I've learned go to waste.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, that's so responsible of you!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Well, haha... Knowledge is power, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: So... full. I'm practically a Blubberbeast, hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Wh—What's that?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: A creature from Fontaine with a super round belly... You've never seen a picture of one?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Aw, it sounds so cute!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can vouch for their cuteness! You can pat their belly, and they'll even join in!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: That reminds me of my saurian companion. Her name was Emela. She wasn't the sharpest Tatankasaur, but she was incredibly brave.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: When there was nothing to do, she would lounge around the tribe without making a sound, even if you bumped into her. Sometimes, visitors would think she was all passed out!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: But, she was completely different once we were on the move. When she was little, I took her on all sorts of adventures. But, saurians grow a lot faster than humans. Before long, she was the one dragging me all over the place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, she must have been a great fighter to keep up with you!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Yeah, she was tough. Varesa told me she was amazing in the final battle...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: I had to defend the Stadium, so... I never got the chance to see her one last time. It was a choice I had to make, but it was hard to accept.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Sorry, I didn't mean to bring down the mood. I'll just get to the important part...

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: I actually saw her in my dreams the past few nights! It felt so real, like it was really her.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: She gave me a ride, and we traveled all around Natlan together. We were both so happy.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Wait, now that you mention it...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I've had dreams of Auntie Atea! She was her typical self — brave and stern, always with that indescribable warmth.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I've never had a dream that felt so real. Just like you said, it felt like I actually got to see her again!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: So, it wasn't just me...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, you've had dreams, too? Don't tell Paimon you dreamt of your aphids or something...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: It wasn't just them. Some of the Gramps and Grannies who looked after me were there, too.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Growing up, I could always hear a degree of guilt in the way they spoke to me. It's why they never asked anything of me, why they gave me so much freedom.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I never wanted things to be that way. But, even in my own dreams, nothing changed... They sounded exactly the same, just like real life.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: The same thing happened to me! I dreamt of Ayo's grandparents.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ayo... Oh, right! Your saurian companion.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Ayo's grandparents fell to the Abyss during the battle... So, it's been really hard for him. He's barely been eating.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I set up a tent near his home so I could be there for him, and I had a dream that his grandparents came back.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I was so happy. In the dream, Ayo seemed like his normal self again. But, it was only for a moment, and then I woke up...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: In real life, Ayo is still struggling. He barely sleeps or eats... But, it's alright! I'll be there for him!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Everyone's had dreams, including me. Could they be related somehow?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}? Chasca? Did you two... Oh, um, sorry. Never mind...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: ...Heh, when did this become story hour?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Still, I have nothing to hide. I dreamt about Chuychu.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: She told me I felt like a completely different person. She said I'm going down the right path, so she doesn't need to pick fights with me anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Maybe your dreams felt real, but the Chuychu I saw was nothing like her "real" self. She would never say anything like that to me.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: It was a dream, nothing more.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Sorry. I shouldn't have brought this up in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: It's fine. I'm the one being a buzzkill...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #W—Well, what about you, {NICKNAME}? Did you have a special dream?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell everyone about your dream, including The Captain and the souls...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: You're kidding! The Captain?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: D—Does that mean you have some kind of secret connection to him?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No! Of course not!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: #Maybe {NICKNAME}'s dream is a different kind of phenomenon...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I may know the cause of the dreams. At the end of the battle, I launched a special kind of Night War by using the power of the divine throne.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Its great power allowed the Ode of Resurrection to bring back all casualties, independent of the time of victory, or the possession of an Ancient Name.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: In addition, the power of the divine throne revitalized the souls and memories within the Night Kingdom, allowing them to take the form of their past selves.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Even after the battle, that effect still lingers. That's why those you lost were able to reappear in your dreams.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: #But, I agree with Ororon... {NICKNAME}'s dream is likely a different matter.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: The shamans of my tribe often receive visions of the future through dreams... Is that what you're suggesting?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Yes, exactly.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #So, {NICKNAME} saw... The Captain's future?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: It's still unclear. But, Granny taught me how to interpret dreams. Would it be okay if I try to take a look?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: If I can observe your soul, I can find out the key elements of the dream.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: For now, you set aside your troubles to savor the delicious food and this happy occasion.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Chasca.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Hello, Archon. I'm fishing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... Doesn't look like the fish are biting today.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Yeah.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: It's okay, you don't have to walk on eggshells around me. I know you can tell I'm not really trying to fish. But, gazing at the water puts me at ease...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I went to visit your parents, Chasca. Of course, I could only offer a few simple condolences...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: You helped a lot, actually. My mom has been doing much better since your visit.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I've always been grateful to my parents for taking me in, but now I have an even deeper sense of responsibility.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I'll never be able to replace Chuychu, but I will do everything in my power to pull them out of their loneliness and despair.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That's exactly what your mother is worried about. She doesn't want you to push yourself to make up for their loss. After all, it's your loss, too.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Grief is not something that can be measured against others. You don't need to make amends, Chasca. Your loss is a tragedy, not a debt.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: In any case, they've always loved both of you. There's no need for you to become Chuychu when they love you just for yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! Don't put too much pressure on yourself!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Thank you, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Sounds like I owe my parents a conversation.

talks.objective: Chat with your friends and wait for the feast to begin
Go to the venue and wait for the feast to begin
Follow Ororon and take part in the ceremony

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I never knew you could make it this way. This formula is new to me...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Your granny never taught you about incense-making?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: No, she usually just lists off the ingredients and tells me to follow the formula...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Haha, then you still have a lot to learn from her.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: #Alright, we're ready, {NICKNAME}. Once you head inside, you'll fall into a brief sleep.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Ororon will interpret the dreamscape, but you won't feel a thing.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: That's right. Everything's all set.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, you just need to take a nap? Sounds easy enough.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See ya later.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Th—This is...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You sleep for a brief period. When you open your eyes again, the ceremony appears to be over.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Here, have some water. It'll help to clear your head.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #You're awake already, {NICKNAME}? That was fast...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It felt like only a few minutes...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: It was enough. What did you learn, Ororon?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: The person next to The Captain... I've seen him before. He was the one who tried to possess me back at the ruin.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? It was him!? Guthred, right? The military doctor?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: So, you know that name, too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! The Captain told us about him when we were helping Iansan.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He was the one who developed the Draught of Lucidity, a drug that can help people with hallucinations.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I see...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: After the battle, I returned to my tribe and began searching through our records of the catastrophe five hundred years ago. Even though my encounter with him was brief, I managed to track down some information...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: The records said he was cold and decisive. Like The Captain, he was formidable in battle, but the two upheld very different ideas of justice.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, he didn't have The Captain's sense of... honor?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That makes sense. The best partners are those who complement each other.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, if there are records of all this, that must mean The Captain was famous in Natlan!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Yes, but unless he brings up his past, few are likely to make the connection between a Fatui Harbinger and Thrain, one of Natlan's legendary heroes.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Guthred is also a respected figure in our nation. The story of how he sacrificed himself for Natlan is a pretty famous tribal legend.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: But, there's still something I don't understand. I'm the only one who saw him. You shouldn't be able to dream of someone you've never met...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: And yet... The figure in your dream looked exactly like him.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: #I don't think that's a coincidence. I believe what {NICKNAME} saw was Guthred's soul.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: But didn't he die hundreds of years ago? There's no way his soul could have survived that long...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe he found his way to the Night Kingdom for a little bit?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: No, the Night Kingdom only accepts the souls of Natlan. It's always been that way. The Ruler of Death likely wanted to prevent the Ode of Resurrection from being abused.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: When I was with The Captain, I could hear something coming from him, souls that were not his own. I heard voices of sorrow and pain, sometimes faint, sometimes strong.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, are you saying The Captain has had Guthred's soul inside of him all along!?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: That's the part I don't understand. Ordinary people shouldn't be able to carry the souls of others...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: It's only possible for me because my situation is unique. And, even then, you saw what happened... The Lord of the Night's voice triggers a violent reaction in those with fragmented souls.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But The Captain didn't react at all.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I even checked his soul myself. It's resilient, radiant, and entirely in one piece.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe it has something to do with Guthred, then...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: It's very possible.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: It's still too early to tell, but the continued existence of Guthred's soul is likely the key to figuring out The Captain's true intentions.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I agree.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Captain never revealed anything to you? The two of you worked together for quite some time...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: No, he rarely talked about himself. We were united in our efforts to save Natlan, but it never went beyond that.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Let's come back to this later. One final step, and we save Natlan for good. That must be our focus.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I'll tell the officials at the Speaker's Chamber to monitor The Captain. Nevertheless, I doubt his goal will interfere with our plan.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, he's definitely up to something, but there are far more important things for Paimon to worry about...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Like, if Paimon had to rate her level of worry... The Captain gets maybe fifty points. But, considering the final battle, you two get at least two thousand!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: In any case, conjecture will only get us so far. It might be more useful for you to ask The Captain directly, Ororon. With any luck, he might just tell you the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Huh? M—Me...?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Don't tell me you haven't noticed his respect for you? The First of the Fatui Harbingers doesn't work with just anyone.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Fortune favors the bold. So, if you ask me, posing the question directly is the wiser choice.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I'm not so sure... But I'll give it a try.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Alright, let's head back and enjoy the party.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After you return, everyone enjoys the gathering until sundown.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: #Thank you so much for coming, everyone! As this gathering comes to a close, let's hear it for the Pyro Archon and {NICKNAME} one last time!

dialogues.speaker: Kinai
dialogues.text: Good luck!

dialogues.speaker: Caipa
dialogues.text: You've got this!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: For Natlan!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Thank you, everyone. Today has meant so much to me. It's been a long time since I had the chance to truly relax.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! Today was great!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you very much.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Well, that concludes the send-off! Everyone is free to go. Any volunteers willing to stick around for clean-up, follow me!

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Oh, I'm in!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Alright, I'm going to head back to the Stadium. I'm sure there's a lot of work to make up at the Speaker's Chamber.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, what happened to taking a break?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: There is no break from the responsibilities of an Archon. Anyone else heading to the Stadium? We can go together.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Yeah, I'll come. There's a few things I want to pick up before I head home. No one really needs a peacemaker right now, so I think I'll spend some time with my parents.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, see you soon!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Time for me to head back, too... Oh, wait! I should stop by Ifa's place first.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I need to make sure he's taking care of my radishes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course you do... Well, safe travels!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I should also get going. Bye for now, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, wait! Paimon wanted to ask something... Where was Ajaw this whole time?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Ajaw's not exactly a good party guest — unless you prefer parties with less food and more insults.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, you put him in a timeout?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Heh, what goes around comes around!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: I'm gonna go, too! Good luck with your Ancient Name!

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Not sure if you already know this, but being the first bearer of your name is a huge honor in Natlan. It comes with a lot of responsibility.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: But, I'm sure your deeds will be remembered for generations to come! I believe in you!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Well, guess I should head out, too. It's gonna be super late by the time I get back...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I think I'll go see Xilonen. She's probably done with your Ancient Name by now. I can check for you!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So soon?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Yeah! Xilonen is an amazing engraver! She usually works really fast, but your ancient name is a special case, so I can't say for sure...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we also don't have anything to do, so why don't we go together?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Oh, it's okay! I'm not alone — Turbo Twirly's with me!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Still, if you want to check on the progress, we should definitely go together! Getting an Ancient Name is such a special moment!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoo, let's go!

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: H—Help! Someone save meeeeee!

choices.text: At this time of night, it's dangerous to go alone.

talks.objective: Follow the path to escort Kachina back to the tribe

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Hey, remember when you first arrived in Natlan? It was still light out, and we traveled on this road together!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: It was the day before the Pilgrimage, and we met up with Kinich and Mualani.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, feels like it was just yesterday!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We've had a lot of adventures.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Yeah! You saved me from the Night Kingdom, you helped us win that battle against the Abyss...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: And the final battle is just around the corner.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We sent you off to battle. Now, you get to do the same.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh, yeah... Hehe, you're right!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I was so nervous the night before the Pilgrimage, but your words of encouragement made me feel a lot better!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I slept so well that night, and earned the best score I've ever had in the Pilgrimage!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: #S—So, if you're nervous, {NICKNAME}, maybe I can encourage you this time...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: *sigh* I've learned so much from you. But, I doubt I can return the favor...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: #Hehe, I knew it! I really look up to your bravery, {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Alright, let's keep going!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Oh, um... D—Don't worry! I'll be rooting for you! And, if you need help, I'll always be first in line!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: I bear the ancient name "Utha{RUBY#[D]Resilience}biti." That means I'll never give up! So, I guess the only piece of advice I can give you is... Don't back down!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, this is where we met Toto, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Yeah, but Toto probably won't be able to come back here for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: During the battle, Toto refused to leave this place. Monsters started closing in, and he got really injured... But, an amazing doctor saved his life!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: The doctor said he refused to leave because of his "territorial instincts." I have a different idea, though...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Toto is a gentle creature — he's not aggressive or territorial. He loves his home and wants to share that with everyone in the area.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I don't like conflict or violence, either — Toto and I are similar in that way. But, we want to protect the things we love from being destroyed. So... we chose to fight.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Love is an extremely positive and powerful emotion, but sometimes it comes with pain — that's what my dad always says.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Now, I finally understand what he meant.

choices.text: You and Toto are both very brave.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: It's alright. This will all be over soon.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: The fact that I was born in this era, that I got to meet legendary heroes like you and our Archon... actually makes me feel really lucky.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: I've always wanted to see what Natlan would be like without the Abyss...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: And now, that day is just around the corner. I know you two can win this!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, it's time to get this over with. We've still got a long journey ahead of us!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: C'mon, we're almost there!

choices.text: I'm sorry you had to grow up so fast.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Wait, that's Hanwi... Hey, Hanwi! What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Oh, let me introduce you — this is Ayo's mom!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello!

dialogues.speaker: Hanwi
dialogues.text: Roar, roar!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Oh no, you seem worried... Is something wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: She left! C'mon, let's follow her!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you two. The party's over, I'm guessing...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You knew about that?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Of course! Everyone in Natlan is rooting for you.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Xilonen is working on the last part of your Ancient Name. It's best not to bother her when she's in the zone.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Your Name is a special case. There were quite a few headaches along the way, which slowed the progress.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This is already faster than I expected.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I told Xilonen, if we hurry, we might make it to the feast in time to snag the last round of barbecue.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I was just teasing, but she gave it some serious thought, nodded, and really hit the ground running after that... It's like my joke lit a fire under her or something.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like she really wanted that barbecue.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Yeah, it's a favorite in her tribe. I bet she still hasn't realized the feast is already over...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, should we go make some for her, then?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, if she's looking forward to it that much.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I appreciate the thought, but there's no need. I can tell what time it is — the light outside is a dead giveaway.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Besides, I knew it was a joke. But, we were having a serious conversation at the time, so I decided to give a serious response.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: *ahem* Anyway, I have something more important to show you. Here, take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: WOW! It's your Ancient Name!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: "Tum{RUBY#[D]Hope}aini"... a name surfaced from the very bottom of the river of souls. It means "hope."

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: A light to guide us through the darkness, like the stars or the moon... It's a perfect fit.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Amazing! Does this name come with a cool chant like the others?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: #Of course, but that'll come later. {NICKNAME} is the first bearer of this name — those words will emerge naturally during {M#his}{F#her} journey.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Once you return triumphant from the battle, I'm sure you will have fully understood why the Lord of the Night chose this name for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, getting this Name turned out to be easier than Paimon was expecting.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: It all came down to the Lord of the Night's power. This situation is the first of its kind. Heck, I doubt we'll ever get a chance like this again.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Imagine receiving that much help from the Lord of the Night only for our most trusted engraver to fail... That would have been so embarrassing for humanity.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Success was never a question. You just like to make things seem dramatic. It's all those novels you read...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hey, it's not like I wanted you to fail! When you've been alive as long as me, you learn that anything can happen!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, okay. It all worked out in the end...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Your Name was successfully forged, and it passed all my technical tests... But there's still one more step.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: We need to make sure the name has accepted you, and will function normally in your possession.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: An outlander has never received an Ancient Name before. I wouldn't be surprised if something equally unprecedented happens when you connect to it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you're saying, it's still too early to celebrate...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, when it comes to something this important, we can't leave anything to chance. Let's run this final test!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Don't worry, the process is simple. We can find a quiet place to test it out after dinner.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Basically, I need to observe whether your soul can connect to the Ley Lines, and make sure there are no signs of rejection.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Last time, you essentially "barged into" the Night Kingdom, but now, we must make sure that it will truly accept you.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Just leave it to me — I'm a professional.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Just like that...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Oh, and you can have the Pilgrim's Chronicle back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? It wasn't destroyed?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: If forging an Ancient Name consumed the memories used to create it, the first person to bear the name would never be remembered.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: The Pilgrim's Chronicle is still the most significant proof of your adventures in Natlan.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thank you.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: No need to make a fuss... Let's go eat. I'm starving.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: C'mon, I'll take you to my favorite barbecue place.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hah, barbecue! See? I knew you couldn't resist!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Oh, I forgot to mention... The place has top-tier alcohol as well.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Well, what are we waiting for? Hop to it, people!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You enjoy a delicious barbecue dinner together. It seems to be Xilonen and Citlali's first meal of the day.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The alcohol is equally delicious, but out of respect for the test that will come next, Citlali only takes a few sips.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After the meal, Xilonen heads back to retrieve her tools while you wait outside with Citlali.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is something on your mind, Citlali? You barely had anything to drink at dinner...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Heh, I didn't think anything could shake me at this age...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: But, the closer we get to the final battle, the more worried I feel... You have an Ancient Name now, but the Ode of Resurrection only takes effect if you win.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: And, the Pyro Archon's fate... is pointing toward "death."

choices.text: No fate is set in stone.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I believe in you... And, thank you — your words mean a lot.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Alright, I'm ready... Oh, is something wrong?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, not at all! Citlali just... ate too much!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Yes, that's right! So, I should really walk it off. C'mon, let's run the final test.

choices.text: Now, we just need to strike.

talks.objective: Talk to Ayo and his family

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Oh, it's because of Ayo. *sigh* Still no change, huh... Poor thing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, right... You said Ayo's grandparents died in the battle.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Yeah. When the Abyss attacked, Ayo's entire family fought to defend our tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Ayo's parents made it through, but his grandparents weren't so lucky...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: The whole family was really close, and now, Ayo barely sleeps or eats. All he wants to do is look for them.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Maybe he thinks his grandparents are still out there somewhere, but there's no bringing them back...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Hey, Ayo... It's me! Feeling any better?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I brought some steak for you. I know it's your favorite, and it's still warm... Want some?

dialogues.speaker: Ayo
dialogues.text: Roar...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Nope. It's like he doesn't even know I'm here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, doesn't this situation remind you of Abyssal Corrosion Syndrome?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Kind of...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Huh? What's Abyssal Corrosion Syndrome?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: According to The Captain, it's a kind of mental disorder that results from Abyssal contamination, even after its power has been purified.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It can cause hallucinations, mental breakdowns... It's really dangerous.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: That does kind of sound like what's happening to Ayo, but I don't think he was contaminated by the Abyss...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's hard to say for sure. Still, Abyssal power was everywhere during the battle. Maybe it affected him indirectly...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: It's possible...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We have a few doses of medicine on us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! That medicine was really effective against the worst cases. Since we don't have any other options, should we give it a try?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Okay, but just a small amount. Since it was developed for humans, it might have a different effect on a saurian.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, better safe than sorry!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After you administer the medicine, Ayo immediately perks up and scarfs down the steak in one bite!

dialogues.speaker: Ayo
dialogues.text: Roar!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: You're okay? I'm so relieved!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Thank you so much! That medicine is amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Hanwi & Anpao
dialogues.text: Roar, roar...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Done eating, Ayo? Then, you should get some rest. You've barely slept these past few days.

dialogues.speaker: Ayo
dialogues.text: Roar, roar!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Okay, okay! You're full of energy, aren't you? Fine, I won't nag you. Just don't overdo it!

dialogues.speaker: Ayo
dialogues.text: Roar, roar!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Thank you so much, you two. You helped save Ayo!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Could you share some of that medicine with me? I want to be able to help someone else if I were to run into a similar situation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Y'know, I used take a lot of things for granted. Growing up, it's easy to think that everything around you will just exist forever.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: But the battle taught me that very few things in life are permanent. Like this path, for example... It's the same one we walked before, but now, the view is completely different.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: It makes the things we love even more precious. So, I want to do as much as I can to defend my family and friends, so I can move forward without regrets.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I feel the same way.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Actually, that's something I learned from you, hehe! You've really taught me a lot.

choices.text: You give me too much credit.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! You're so talented and strong — practically a star pupil!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: R—Really? So, you think I'm doing a good job? I've been a good... disciple? Or, uh, student? Or, um...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How about... friend?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: *tearful whimper*...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Thank you! I... I won't let you down! I'll train even harder tomorrow!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Hehe, alright, we're not far from the tribe. Let's go.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Bye, Ayo! Bye, Hanwi! Bye, Anpao!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Phew, we're here! That was quite the trek.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: After you visit Xilonen, you should come over for dinner! You can stay the night, too. I'll help my parents get everything ready!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We wouldn't want to impose...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's see how things go with Xilonen first.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Totally up to you! You're always welcome!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Bye!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: When you think about it, we haven't actually known Kachina that long...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Our journey in Natlan feels like it just started, and now it's about to end.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There are still a lot of places we haven't seen.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's true! We'll just have to add them to the itinerary!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, time to go check on our... *ahem* your ancient name!

talks.objective: Check on how the forging of the Ancient Name is going
Test the Ancient Name outside the camp

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: All set, Xilonen?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Just need to check one more thing, and... Yeah, okay! We're good!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Alright, I'll stand next to you and monitor your connection to the Ley Lines. It shouldn't take long, but you need to look out for one thing.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: This test relies on the same principles as the Spiritspeaker Stone. I heard about what happened when you used it last time...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah! Abyssal power kept surging out! If Chasca hadn't destroyed the stone, Vichama would have been consumed by the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: That's exactly what I'm worried about. All this time, our final foe has continued to corrode the Ley Lines from the depths of the Night Kingdom.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Your resistance to its power is remarkable, but you need to tell me if anything feels wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: If either of us notices something off, the test ends, got it?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Don't worry, I'll use Elemental power to take care of that. This isn't exactly a picnic in the park, but everyone knows you never leave trash behind.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Xilonen, I'm ready to start.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Paimon, give us a little more space.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, okay!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Let's do this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, that light is beautiful! It's exactly like when we used the Spiritspeaker Stone.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Your connection to the Ley Lines looks good... I can sense the Lord of the Night.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Your soul is remarkable. Such a strong presence... even on par with the Lord of the Night.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Looks like the Lord of the Night has accepted this Name and acknowledged you as its bearer... No surprise there, considering we only got this far because of her.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Stable connection to the Ley Lines, no unexpected fluctuations... Both good signs.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: #How do you feel, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Then, it looks like your Ancient Name is good to go. That's great news.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, look! Something's coming!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: No need to panic, Paimon. The damage to the Ley Lines has allowed these soul-like beings to leak out onto the surface.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: It's just because of the ritual. It makes it so that everyone can see them. I know they look like ghosts, but it shouldn't last long...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: A—Although, there shouldn't be this many!

response.speaker: Olaya
response.text: Home...

response.speaker: Cahuia
response.text: This... way...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Xilonen, stop the test! We've already confirmed what we came here for!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Got it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What's going on?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I see... It wasn't just escaped souls. The ritual attracted all the souls in the surrounding area.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Surrounding area?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: The Night Kingdom is getting weaker by the day, especially in its capacity to accept souls. After death, many souls fail to return to the Ley Lines.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Once a soul becomes lost, it can never return to the Night Kingdom. Lost souls can only wander listlessly, gradually fading from existence before disappearing entirely.

response.speaker: Poloa
response.text: Please... Take me back...

response.speaker: Zumalli
response.text: I... cannot... disappear...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: So, the connection we established to the Night Kingdom... That's what drew them here?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: #Yes. {NICKNAME}'s soul is powerful, so the echoes coming back from the Night Kingdom were loud and strong...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Some of these souls never made it to the Ley Lines, others escaped from the Night Kingdom, and even more don't even come from Natlan... Complicated doesn't even begin to describe it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: S—So, they've always been around? We just couldn't see them most of the time?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Can we save them?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: We can try. Returning souls to the Ley Lines usually requires a complex ritual. But, we don't have time for that, and neither do they...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: That's exactly why my people turned to "vessels" like Ororon.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: He has a remarkable ability to perceive souls. Even after the failed ceremony, he made it his mission to travel around Natlan and return as many souls as possible.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: But, most of the time, having the ability to perceive souls means watching them wither away in agony, completely powerless to stop it...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: So you're saying... There will always be those that we can't save?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: That's right, but saving some is still better than saving none at all. After all, souls that disappear can never be reborn...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: That has to be true loneliness... The knowledge that you've been abandoned by the world, even in death...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Then, we have to do something.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! We should try to save whoever we can!

choices.text: I'm more worried about Abyssal power leaking out.

talks.objective: Talk to the soul that suddenly appeared

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: V—Vichama!? Is that you!?

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: Oh... I know you.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: I didn't think we would meet again, especially like this.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: Using the Spiritspeaker Stone meant so much to me... Thank you, Citlali. I finally have the chance to say that in person.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Enough of that... What happened to you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You... didn't make it through the battle?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, you're from the Scions of the Canopy! During the battle, your tribe was...!

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: It's okay. The battle finally gave me the chance to fulfill my dream.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: Back then, I missed my chance at the Night Warden Wars. I wasn't about to let that happen twice.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: I scouted the location and direction of the attacks, so I could tell Chief Wayna the safest way to evacuate.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: Those with grappling hooks escaped through the air. Everyone else banded together on the ground to break through the front.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: But, people needed information, so I stayed behind until the very end.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: ...You're a true hero.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: Thank you, but that's not why I did it.... I did it for the future of my tribe and the future of Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: The battle gave me back my sense of purpose. That's all I wanted.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: And, anyway, I was supposed to see Mallko again. I thought we would witness Natlan's rebirth together...

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: But the Night Kingdom rejected me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Even though you're a hero of Natlan? How could that happen?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I'm sorry... The Lord of the Night didn't do it on purpose, I can promise you that. The Ley Lines are in terrible shape. Even the Ode of Resurrection is no longer working like it should...

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: I know... She can't help it, right?

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: I get it. It just feels like fate is mocking me. Even in death... I won't ever get to be with Mallko again.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: No, it hasn't been long since the battle. The door to the Night Kingdom should still be open to you.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Give me some time. I'll think of something.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: I—Is that even possible?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It doesn't matter — I have to try. A hero of Natlan deserves a better fate than this!

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: This feeling... Is this the Night Kingdom?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Phew... Looks like this method worked on you.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: Thank you... Thank you so much! People don't always have the nicest things to say about you... But, shows what they know...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hmph, that's a given.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I hope you come back to us soon, Vichama.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: If I may... What about the others? Can you save them, too?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: Don't apologize. You're doing everything you can. This isn't anyone's fault.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: Let this land bear witness to my final wish for this world...

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: From now on, may every soul in Natlan find haven and home.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I promise you, Vichama — I will not abandon the Ley Lines to their fate.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Leave it to us.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: Thank you... People like you are the true heroes.

dialogues.speaker: Vichama
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

talks.objective: Talk to the souls that suddenly appeared

dialogues.speaker: Cahuia
dialogues.text: Home... Here... Home...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: She's one of the souls that overflowed from the Night Kingdom. She can no longer go back there.

dialogues.speaker: Cahuia
dialogues.text: Home... Home...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're sorry... If there was anything we could do...

dialogues.speaker: Cahuia
dialogues.text: Home...

dialogues.speaker: Cahuia
dialogues.text: Ho...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: She's at her limit. Just getting here has taken all her strength.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Poloa
dialogues.text: Let me go back... Let me go...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The Night Kingdom isn't responding. *sigh* That means its doors are closed...

dialogues.speaker: Poloa
dialogues.text: Why...

dialogues.speaker: Poloa
dialogues.text: I... fought... my entire life... I... believed... the Lord of the Night... would...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I'm sorry. The Ley Lines are overwhelmed, and the Lord of Night has no strength left...

dialogues.speaker: Poloa
dialogues.text: Why... me...?

dialogues.speaker: Poloa
dialogues.text: Who... am I?

dialogues.speaker: Poloa
dialogues.text: Does it even matter... who I am...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course you matter! Wait!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He's gone.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Absolute helplessness... that's what he felt in his final moments. I could sense it.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I'm sorry...

talks.objective: Talk to the souls that suddenly appeared

dialogues.speaker: Ayele
dialogues.text: Save me...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I can help you. Just hold on.

dialogues.speaker: Ayele
dialogues.text: The... Night Kingdom...

dialogues.speaker: Ayele
dialogues.text: Thank you...

dialogues.speaker: Ayele
dialogues.text: You must be from the Masters of the Night-Wind. Would you tell me your name, kind soul?
