dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Citlali.

dialogues.speaker: Ayele
dialogues.text: Cit... lali...

dialogues.speaker: Ayele
dialogues.text: What a beautiful name...

dialogues.speaker: Ayele
dialogues.text: Dazzling... just like the stars in the sky.

dialogues.speaker: Zumalli
dialogues.text: I... can't... disappear...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It hasn't been long since he died. I can still try to save him!

dialogues.speaker: Zumalli
dialogues.text: I... can't...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Watch out, Citlali! The Abyss is corrupting him!

dialogues.speaker: Zumalli
dialogues.text: ■■...disappearing...you ■■...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I'm sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: The Abyss has corrupted his soul from the inside. Even if we could send him back to the Night Kingdom, it would only make the situation worse.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I know. If we were just a little quicker, we could have stripped away its power...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...But, it's too late. Let's go check on the others.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no... Saurian souls can be affected, too?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Their souls are still intact... I should be able to help them.
Roar, roar...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hold on, is that...!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ayo?

dialogues.speaker: Ayo
dialogues.text: Roar...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: That's right, I recognize him, and the two souls next to him should be his grandparents. Kachina told me about what happened.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: It all makes sense now. Ayo could barely sleep or eat because he sensed the presence of his grandparents.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That must be why he looks so happy right now — they're finally reunited.

dialogues.speaker: Ayo
dialogues.text: Roar, roar...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: When was the last time Ayo slept?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: From what Kachina said, it's been a while. He hasn't been doing so hot lately.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, now that he's seen his grandparents again, he looks completely at ease.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Kachina's taken me to meet Ayo before. He's always been such an energetic little saurian. If he didn't want to sleep, even his parents couldn't make him.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: But, whenever his grandparents started to sing to him, he would fall asleep in no time.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I think it's a song from when Ayo's father was a baby, or even before then.

dialogues.speaker: Cetan
dialogues.text: Roar, roar, roar...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's amazing... Ayo was so restless earlier, and now he's completely calm.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ayo can finally get a good night's sleep.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still... It's not like this can go on forever.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: No, their time is running out... I have to send them back to the Night Kingdom before it's too late.

dialogues.speaker: Hnaska
dialogues.text: Rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Cetan
dialogues.text: Roar, roar!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What's wrong with them? They got super angry all of a sudden...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: They don't want to go.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I know you don't want to leave Ayo, but you can't stay here. You're running out of time.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: If you don't go back to the Night Kingdom now, you'll disappear in a few days!

dialogues.speaker: Hnaska
dialogues.text: Rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Cetan
dialogues.text: Roar, rawr!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: They've made their position clear.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: "We want to stay by his side, no matter what."

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: *sigh*...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: We should respect their decision.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I don't want to leave them to that fate... But, if this is what they want, then I can't separate them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What fate? You mean, like the other lost souls?

dialogues.speaker: Cetan
dialogues.text: Roar, roar, roar.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Yes... They will gradually fade away, painfully and slowly, until nothing is left.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But, that is their choice. For the next few days... At least Ayo will get a good night's sleep.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We must save the Ley Lines.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: That's the only way to prevent more souls from suffering the same fate.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Once all traces of Abyssal power are removed from the Night Kingdom, the Pyro Archon will restore the Ley Lines — that's the final step of her plan.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So we're not just fighting for the living, but for the dead, too...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That reminds me of the dream I had about The Captain...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: What dream?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh yeah, you said The Captain had a bunch of these kinds of souls with him. Maybe they're looking for a home, too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...But, it's impossible for Khaenri'ahns to enter the Night Kingdom, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Although, it wouldn't be the first time The Captain tried to do the impossible.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Even in its fully functional state, the Night Kingdom can't accept foreign souls. It's completely isolated from the Ley Lines of other nations.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: In theory, that means Khaenri'ahn souls shouldn't be drawn to the presence of the Night Kingdom. Something strange is going on...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: One thing's for sure — it seems like The Captain wants to help these souls.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, he usually keeps his cards close to his chest. If we want to know what he's up to, we just have to wait for him to act.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, let's focus on the final battle. That's the most important thing right now.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I will.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Good or bad, happy or cruel, we always have to face the truth. Reality doesn't change just because we choose not to face it.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I just wish I could have done more. So many souls, and I could barely help. I'm so sorry...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, don't apologize! None of this was your fault.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I guess you're right... If we want to end this, we have to tackle the root of the problem — the Ley Lines.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: It's just another reason why this battle is so important.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, before you set off, remember to give your Ancient Name to the Pyro Archon. She will introduce it to our people and explain its meaning.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Then, the rest is up to you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And don't forget — we're all cheering for you!

choices.text: I'll try to remember everything I've learned on my journey.
We should probably mention Ayo's grandparents to Kachina.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Huh, still no label... If I want to know who sent this, guess the box will be my only clue.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: The Pyro Archon is right. I still have a long way to go, but I will have time to grow.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Alright, break time! Get some water, and let me know if you start to feel dizzy.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: I'll take things from here.

dialogues.speaker: Kinai
dialogues.text: If we don't solve the crisis in the Night Kingdom, war will continue to ravage our nation.

dialogues.speaker: Kinai
dialogues.text: We've achieved a brief moment of peace, but we can't get complacent. Even if it's not on the front lines, there are still things we can do.

dialogues.speaker: Kinai
dialogues.text: Like fortifying our defenses, eliminating remaining monsters, rebuilding our homes...

dialogues.speaker: Kinai
dialogues.text: And coming together like this to sing for you and offer our warmest blessings.

dialogues.speaker: Caipa
dialogues.text: Archon, what is it like in the depths of the Night Kingdom? We really can't go with you?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: No, that region has been completely corroded by the Abyss. Without protection, an ordinary person would not last a minute.

dialogues.speaker: Caipa
dialogues.text: Oh... I guess we'd only get in your way... Then, this really is a battle reserved for the gods.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Fear not — I've been preparing for this moment a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: This duty is mine to bear, and I will succeed.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Thank you for everything you said. I'll talk to my parents soon.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: You've got me curious about this dream, too! Be sure to come back and tell us what you learn!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Yeah! And let us know if you need any help!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Little Kinich, think you can lock me away forever? Heh, we'll see who gets the last laugh!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, this is where we met Toto, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Yeah, but Toto probably won't be able to come back here for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: During the battle, Toto refused to leave this place. Monsters started closing in, and he got really injured... But, an amazing doctor saved his life!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, we saw him during the battle... Thank goodness he made it!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: The doctor said he refused to leave because of his "territorial instincts." I have a different idea, though...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Toto is a gentle creature — he's not aggressive or territorial. He loves his home and wants to share that with everyone in the area.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I don't like conflict or violence, either — Toto and I are similar in that way. But, we want to protect the things we love from being destroyed. So... we chose to fight.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Love is an extremely positive and powerful emotion, but sometimes it comes with pain — that's what my dad always says.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Now, I finally understand what he meant.

choices.text: You and Toto are both very brave.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: It's alright. This will all be over soon.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: The fact that I was born in this era, that I got to meet legendary heroes like you and our Archon... actually makes me feel really lucky.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: I've always wanted to see what Natlan would be like without the Abyss...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: And now, that day is just around the corner. I know you two can win this!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, it's time to get this over with. We've still got a long journey ahead of us!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: C'mon, we're almost there!

choices.text: I'm sorry you had to grow up so fast.
